summary: Security spine is sound. Hash-only key lookup (no plaintext/timing oracle on the secret), uniform 401 across all three key causes (no enumeration), project-scoped subscriber resolution from the key (anti-IDOR, cross-project collapses to 404), CSRF correctly disabled on the STATELESS header-key chain, CORS uses a single explicit origin (not wildcard) with credentials, rate-limit DoS bound paired with the Redis-independent fan-out ceiling, and no key/hash/PII in logs. No critical or high findings.

findings.finding: Project is resolved from the API key (no path projectId). subscriber_id lookup is filtered by the key's projectId (findById(projectId,id) -> filter sub.projectId==projectId); telegram_user_id lookup is keyed by (projectId, telegramUserId). A subscriber in another tenant collapses to 404. Verified by events_crossProjectSubscriberId_returns404.

Every key fault (missing/blank/malformed/unknown) takes one code path -> sendError(401) with no body. lookup() does a single hashed lookup (no plaintext compare), so there is no timing oracle on the secret. Uniform 401 asserted byte-identical across all three causes.
No API key, key hash, event_name, or subscriber PII is logged anywhere; only projectId/subscriberId/exception-class. Matches Decision 16 PII rule.

stampLastUsedAt issues a Mongo save() on every authenticated request, an attacker with a valid key could drive a write per request. The global /events rate-limit (429) bounds it; the stamp is also after the key is already proven valid.
findings.reason: Bounded by the 300/min global rate-limit and gated on a valid key. The task explicitly requires stamping lastUsedAt per authenticated call. Acceptable; throttling/debouncing the stamp is a possible future optimization, out of scope here.

findings.finding: event_name is slug-validated (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$); telegram_user_id is typed Long; subscriber_id is passed as a String _id through Spring Data findById (parameterized, no injection; a non-existent id returns empty, no exception for String @Id).
findings.reason: Inputs validated/typed at the boundary; no injection surface.

findings.finding: CSRF disabled only on the STATELESS /api/integrations/** header-key chain (no ambient cookie auth to forge). CORS adds X-API-Key to allowedHeaders with a single explicit allowed origin (app.url) and allowCredentials=true — not a wildcard, so the credentialed-CORS pitfall is avoided.
findings.reason: Correct scoping; session chain CSRF unchanged.
